//: tsx's default JSX transform is the CLASSIC one (React.createElement), and
the app's own tsconfig says `jsx: preserve` because Next compiles it. A
check that renders a component therefore needs its own compiler options —
this file, passed with --tsconfig. It is NOT the app's build config and
must never be referenced by next.config or by tsc --noEmit.
It lives at the REPO ROOT and not in scripts/checks/ for one reason: tsx
applies a --tsconfig only to files under that config's own directory, and
the check renders components that live in forge-control-web/app. A config
inside scripts/ left those on the classic transform and they crashed with
`React is not defined`. Root is the only directory above both trees.
Run (from forge-control-web, whose node_modules holds react/react-dom):
//paths: A check script lives in scripts/checks/, which has no node_modules — so a
bare `react` / `react-dom/server` import resolves nowhere, no matter which
directory the process was started from. These four mappings point at the
web app's installed copies (tsx honours tsconfig paths). Same physical
package the app itself loads; nothing is installed for the check.
